svg.text: Two choices, two entailments — a psyche is built, not picked from a list
GRAYSCALE STRUCTURE WIREFRAME — no colour, no final type, no motion

g.text: THE EIGHT — CHOOSING THE AUXILIARY; 6 ARE NOW ILLEGAL
Law I — the top two face opposite worlds. Law II — the top two do opposite
jobs. Together those leave exactly two legal auxiliaries per dominant. 8 x
THE VESSEL — TWO CROSSED AXES, FOUR SLOTS
radius = rank · distance from core = pressure · open ring = not yet placed
Stress 0 on all four. Capacity full. State BALANCED. A vessel keeps its
wear across scenario runs in this session, so the second scenario is
OR TAKE A FINISHED TYPE — THE SAME SIXTEEN, DERIVED NOT STORED
THE ENTAILMENT BEAT — SLOTS 3 AND 4 ARE NOT CHOICES, AND THE INTERFACE MUST NOT PRETEND THEY ARE

When the auxiliary lands, slots 3 and 4 fill themselves by Law III (every function installs its polar opposite at the far end of its axis). Those two placements animate as consequences, not selections: no affordance, no cursor change, a
one-line explanation each. This is the single most teachable fact in typology and it is free — it only requires that we refuse to draw four identical drop targets.
Ti dominant → Fe is installed inferior (judgment axis). Se auxiliary → Ni is installed tertiary (perception axis).

svg.text: CALLOUT LEGEND — WHAT THE REGION DOES · HOV ON HOVER · CMT ON COMMIT · L/G UNDER LOOP OR GRIP
Step ribbon — two choices, two entailments
Four steps, but only steps 1 and 2 are interactive. Steps 3 and 4 are drawn in a permanently non-interactive style
(dashed, no fill, no hover) because they are consequences of steps 1–2.
Steps 3–4 give no hover response at all — a deliberate dead affordance.
Placing the auxiliary advances all three remaining steps at once.
Not present; assembly precedes any simulation state.
The eight — dominant chooser, then legality filter
All eight are live at step 1. Once a dominant is placed, six of the eight are struck out and labelled ILLEGAL with
the law that excludes them; the two legal auxiliaries are given a heavier border.
An illegal tile explains which of Law I / Law II it violates instead of doing nothing.
Selecting a legal tile writes slot 2 and triggers the entailment beat.
The radial layout from layout Strategy B, relocated here where gestalt matters more than precise comparison. Slot
radius encodes rank; distance from the ego core encodes pressure; an open dashed ring means unplaced.
Hovering a slot dims the other three and names the axis it belongs to.
Placement fills the ring and snaps the glyph to solid ink.
The same figure is reused as the S6 aggregate; loop and grip redraw its conduits.
The aggregate point. Empty during assembly; in S6 it carries the whole-human readouts and shifts toward whichever
Grip drags the core toward the inferior slot; loop draws a lit path that visibly skips the auxiliary.
Names the type as soon as it is determined, and names the counterfactual (“picking Ni instead gives INTP”) so the
user sees that one click separates two types.
Hovering a stack row previews that function’s info page glyph at full size.
States the starting condition of the vessel. Critical because vessels persist across scenario runs in a session:
this strip is where a returning user learns they are re-entering with wear.
If the vessel is already in Loop or Grip from a previous run, that is declared here, before scenario choice.
Single exit. Disabled and visibly so until slot 2 exists. There is no way to reach a scenario with an incomplete
Escape hatch for users who already know their type. Shows the derived stack under each code so the preset still
Previews the stack into the Vessel figure without committing.
Fills all four slots and skips the entailment beat.
Permanent footer, not a dismissible tooltip. It is the lesson the screen exists to teach, so it does not hide.
Three laws stated in one block, adjacent to the grid they are currently constraining. Placed next to the cause,
Inferior slot — smallest radius, furthest out
Drawn smallest and furthest from the core. This is the only screen where the inferior is visually minor; every
later screen lets it grow, and in Grip (S8) it becomes the largest thing on screen.
Grip inflates this slot past the dominant.
Dominant slot — largest radius, nearest core
Radius and proximity both encode rank, so the hierarchy survives greyscale, small sizes, and colour-blindness.
Rank is never carried by colour anywhere in this system.
Loop keeps this slot lit; Grip demotes it.

Structure phase, grayscale by discipline. Colour, type scale, glyph artwork and motion curves are deferred to the visual-design phase; tick tuning, persistence and the text corpus are deferred to implementation. Both deferral lists are
enumerated in 00-BRIEF.md section 5 and BUILD-SPEC.md section 9. Worked type: ISTP (Ti / Se / Ni / Fe). Worked scenario: The Credit Thief.
